eShop legacy (.NET Framework 4.7.2) vs .NET 8: end-to-end parity report

Integration branch devin/hcl-net8-eshop at b93a0b1 (devin/hcl-net8-eshop 8686730 + parity fixes of PR #91); generated by modernization/parity/report/gen_report.py.

1. Executive summary

620 / 620flow replays at parity across 4 runs (155 flows x mock, SQL, mock-container, SQL-container)
0failing flows in the final runs
94 / 94per-flow data-state checks equal after mutating flows (pages and/or sqlcmd dumps; 30 mutating flows per run, unchecked ones covered by the end-of-sequence snapshots, all equal)
2 found, 2 fixedregressions (SQL-mode WebForms edit + save-time validation), PR #91
4known divergences per run, all host 404 error-page bodies (status equal)
170 / 170.NET 8 tests passed (2 skips = SQL-only tests without a server; 51/51 with SQL)

The legacy apps (.NET Framework 4.7.2 code built and hosted on Mono 6.12 + xsp4, because the VM has no Windows/IIS) and the migrated ASP.NET Core 8 apps were run side by side and every one of the 155 recorded transcripts was replayed live against both, in lockstep, with both sides restarted before every mutation sequence.

Mock mode: 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known; 17/17 per-flow data-state checks (page snapshots where the baseline took them; the other 13 mutating flows are not re-rendered to keep mock navigation properties cold, Q4) and 9/9 end-of-sequence snapshots equal. Same result against the .NET 8 Linux container images: 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known.

SQL mode: legacy MVC and WebForms (EF6 on Mono) and .NET 8 (EF Core 8) each seeded a fresh database in the same SQL Server 2022 container from their own initializer. The first round found 6 failing flows from 2 root causes, both in the migrated WebForms SQL path; after the fix: 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known, 30/30 per-flow data-state checks equal including sqlcmd dumps of both databases after every mutating flow. Container SQL profile (compose images and their own sqldata container, sqlcmd dumps of both databases): 29 identical + 122 equivalent + 4 known, 30/30 per-flow data-state checks equal.

Every remaining difference is classified in section 10. Open regressions: 0. Not verified here: Windows/IIS hosting of the legacy apps, and a recorded manual UI walkthrough (see section 11).

2. Scope

Migrated (in scope)

  • Legacy MVC catalog (eShopLegacyMVCSolution/src/eShopLegacyMVC): list with paging, details, create, edit, delete, picture route items/{id}/pic, Web API /api/brands (GET/DELETE) and /api/files, session footer -> eShopNet8/src/eShopNet8.Mvc.
  • Legacy WebForms catalog (eShopLegacyWebFormsSolution/src/eShopLegacyWebForms): Default.aspx list/paging, Catalog/Create|Edit|Details|Delete.aspx, About, Contact -> Razor Pages in eShopNet8/src/eShopNet8.WebForms.
  • Data: EF6 + HiLo id generator + CatalogDBInitializer -> EF Core 8 with HiLo sequences and the same PreconfiguredData seed (eShopNet8/src/eShop.Catalog.Infrastructure); UseMockData toggle preserved (CatalogServiceMock vs EF CatalogService).
  • Autofac -> built-in DI; log4net -> ILogger; Linux containers on mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:8.0, compose mock and SQL profiles, health endpoints, GitHub Actions CI.

Not migrated / out of scope

  • eShopPorted, eShopModernized* and the N-tier folders (not the migration source).
  • The never-discovered CatalogController2 (Q1): /api stays 404 as in legacy.
  • Windows/IIS-specific hosting (Web.config transforms, IIS modules): replaced by Kestrel + containers.
  • Picture upload (legacy UI says "Uploading images not allowed for this version").

4. Method

  1. Seed data: both sides use the same PreconfiguredData (12 items, 5 brands, 4 types). Mock mode uses each side's in-memory mock; SQL mode drops and re-creates each database so each initializer seeds it (EF6 CatalogDBInitializer on legacy, EF Core seeding on .NET 8).
  2. Replay: sidebyside.py walks the 155 baseline flows in their 13 sequences. Before each sequence that mutates data both sides are restarted (SQL: database dropped and re-seeded). Each flow is sent to legacy and migrated with per-side cookie jars; WebForms postbacks re-harvest that side's own form fields (antiforgery/ViewState) so the same user input is posted to both.
  3. Diffs: each response is normalised per modernization/CONTRACT.md (status, Location, content type family, HTML text/structure/title, JSON, binary hash; masked session footer; >=500 bodies opaque) and compared three ways: legacy-live vs recorded baseline, migrated-live vs baseline, migrated-live vs legacy-live (the verdict). A different pair fails unless it is a documented divergence in known-divergences.json whose reasons all match (status changes are never accepted).
  4. Data state: after every mutating flow the catalog is dumped from both sides; in SQL mode both databases are additionally dumped with sqlcmd (items incl. brand/type names, brands, types; ordered by id) and compared field by field. End-of-sequence snapshots compare the rendered catalog list pages.
  5. Containers: the same replay was run against the .NET 8 images from eShopNet8/docker-compose.yml (profile mock, and profile sql with its own sqldata service; data state from the app pages).
  6. Tests: dotnet test eShopNet8/eShopNet8.sln (Release) with and without ESHOP_TEST_SQL_CONNECTION; the legacy side has no test project, so the transcript suite replayed against live legacy is its test suite.
  7. Screenshots: screenshots.py against legacy mock (5100/5101) and .NET 8 mock (5200/5201).

10. Every difference

IDFlows / modesCategoryRoot causeStatus
R-01wf-edit-postback-valid (+ cascaded data-state diffs in wf-edit-after-details, wf-edit-postback-price-nonnumeric) - SQL mode onlyregressionRound 1: legacy 302, .NET 8 500. The Razor Pages Edit handler loads the item with FindCatalogItem (EF Core tracks it) and then passes a separately bound CatalogItem with the same key to UpdateCatalogItem, which did db.Entry(item).State = Modified -> EF Core InvalidOperationException (another instance with the same key is already tracked). EF6 on legacy tolerated the pattern. File: eShopNet8/src/eShop.Catalog.Infrastructure/Data/CatalogService.cs (UpdateCatalogItem), caller eShopNet8/src/eShopNet8.WebForms/Pages/Catalog/Edit.cshtml.cs.Fixed in https://github.com/COG-GTM/eShopModernizing/pull/91: the already-tracked copy is detached before the posted entity is attached. Unit test Update_after_find_in_the_same_scope_replaces_the_tracked_copy. SQL replay after fix: parity, data state equal.
R-02wf-create-postback-stock-out-of-range (+ cascaded data-state diffs in wf-create-postback-price-nonnumeric, wf-create-postback-no-viewstate) - SQL mode onlyregressionRound 1: legacy 500, .NET 8 302 and the row was saved. Q8 means the WebForms validators do not block the postback, but in SQL mode legacy EF6 DbContext.SaveChanges validates DataAnnotations (DbEntityValidationException for Stock 20000000 > 10 million) so nothing is stored; EF Core performs no save-time validation. The WebForms model has its own annotations (eShopLegacyWebFormsSolution/src/eShopLegacyWebForms/Models/CatalogItem.cs, Q9: Name not required, wide Price range) that differ from MVC's. Files: eShopNet8/src/eShop.Catalog.Infrastructure/Data/CatalogService.cs.Fixed in https://github.com/COG-GTM/eShopModernizing/pull/91: ICatalogItemSaveValidator runs before Add/Update in the EF service (MVC annotations by default, WebFormsCatalogItemSaveValidator with the legacy WebForms annotations registered by the Razor Pages app). Tests Save_validates_the_legacy_annotations_like_EF6_and_stores_nothing and WebFormsSaveValidationTests. SQL replay after fix: parity, data state equal.
D-01mvc-unknown-path (all 4 runs)harness/runtime artifactStatus 404 equal; legacy body is the Mono/xsp4 host HttpException error page (Mono version + stack trace), ASP.NET Core returns an empty 404. Host-generated, not app code. eShopNet8/tests/eShopNet8.IntegrationTests/Parity/known-divergences.json.Accepted (documented known divergence)
D-02mvc-api-root-undiscovered (all 4 runs)harness/runtime artifact/api stays 404 on both (Q1, legacy CatalogController2 never discovered); only the Mono host 404 page body differs.Accepted (documented known divergence)
D-03mvc-pic-nonnumeric (all 4 runs)harness/runtime artifact/items/abc/pic does not match items/{catalogItemId:int}/pic: 404 on both; Mono host error page body differs.Accepted (documented known divergence)
D-04wf-unknown-path (all 4 runs)harness/runtime artifactUnmapped WebForms URL: 404 and content type equal; Mono/xsp4 host error page text differs from the Razor Pages 404.Accepted (documented known divergence)
H-01wf-create-* (SQL container run with both compose services up): wf-create-postback-valid, wf-create-after-list, wf-create-after-details, wf-create-postback-name-missing, wf-create-postback-stock-out-of-range, wf-create-postback-price-nonnumeric, wf-create-postback-no-viewstateharness/runtime artifactIn the compose SQL profile webforms-sql depends_on mvc-sql, so both .NET 8 apps share one DB and mvc-sql seeds it first; the WebForms process then takes a fresh HiLo block and the created item gets id 21 instead of legacy's 13 (legacy is replayed one app per DB). The id shift cascades into the data-state diff and into wf-create-after-details (it requests the legacy id 13 -> Q7 500). Same rows otherwise. Observed in two container runs (7 and 7 failing).Not a product difference (HiLo blocks are per process by design, legacy EF6 HiLo behaves the same). Final container SQL run uses NET8_DOCKER_SOLO=1 (start-net8.sh: up --no-deps, one app at a time) and is reported in section 5.
L-01SQL mode, legacy-live vs recorded (mock) baseline: mvc-details-cold-12, mvc-delete-cold-10, mvc-index-negative-page, mvc-index-negative-size, mvc-edit-post-unknown-id, mvc-delete-post-unknown-idpre-existing legacy defectLegacy itself behaves differently in SQL mode (Q18, BASELINE.md section 5): EF lazy loading fills cold navigation properties; negative paging and POST unknown id throw (500) in EF but not in the mock. The .NET 8 app reproduces each identically (pair verdict equivalent).Reproduced identically (deliberately preserved)
L-02SQL mode, WebForms legacy-live vs mock baseline: wf-index-* / wf-details-found* / wf-edit-found / wf-delete-found / *-warm-list (prices rendered 19.50 instead of 19.5), wf-details-cold-1 and wf-delete-cold-3 (200 instead of 500), wf-index-negative-page (500), wf-create-postback-stock-out-of-range (500)pre-existing legacy defectFirst observation of legacy WebForms in SQL mode (new in this stage): SQL decimal(18,2) keeps scale 2 so Price.ToString() renders 19.50; lazy loading avoids the cold-mock NRE (Q4); EF Skip with a negative count throws; EF6 save-time validation (see R-02). Legacy mode differences, extension of Q18 to WebForms. .NET 8 reproduces each identically.Reproduced identically (deliberately preserved)
S-01mvc-api-files (Q2)intentional/security divergenceLegacy /api/files serialises with BinaryFormatter (CWE-502 deserialisation risk, removed from .NET 8). The .NET 8 app keeps the endpoint shape with a safe replacement; the replay compares it equivalent after normalisation and BinaryFormatterTests assert BinaryFormatter is not used.Intentional, documented in INVENTORY.md Q2 (no observable pair difference)
Q-PREQ3 mvc-api-brand-delete-*; Q4 *-cold-*; Q5 mvc-index-size0, wf-index-size0, wf-index-nonnumeric; Q6 mvc-delete-post-unknown-id; Q7 wf-details-missing, wf-details-aspx-no-route, wf-edit-missing, wf-delete-missing, wf-delete-after-details; Q8 wf-create-postback-*; Q9/Q11/Q13/Q15/Q16 markup and XML negotiationpre-existing legacy defectLegacy defects catalogued in modernization/INVENTORY.md (DELETE /api/brands no-op 200, cold mock navigation properties, pageSize=0 divide-by-zero, unknown ids 500, WebForms ModelState vs Page.IsValid, annotation drift, pager count, stray &lt;/a&gt;, XML content negotiation). Kept on purpose so the migration is behaviour-preserving; every one replays at parity.Reproduced identically (deliberately preserved); candidates for post-migration fixes

K-02sql-container runknown limitationIn the container SQL run the .NET 8 apps use the compose profile's own sqldata container (host port 1434), so the legacy DB (host SQL Server 2022 container, port 1433) and the .NET 8 DB are in two containers from the same image rather than one; sqlcmd dumps of both were taken after every mutating flow (--sql-server-net8 127.0.0.1,1434) and were equal. The single-container requirement is met by the local SQL run.Accepted (compose profile owns its SQL Server)

11. Verified parity vs known limitations

Verified parity (observed in this run)

  • All 155 flows (99 MVC, 56 WebForms) at parity in mock mode, local processes and Linux container images: status, redirects, content types, normalised HTML/JSON/binary bodies.
  • All 155 flows at parity in SQL mode against independent databases seeded by each side's own initializer, with sqlcmd dumps of both databases equal after all 30 mutating flows.
  • HiLo id assignment, create/edit/delete persistence, paging, details/edit/delete pages, MVC server-side validation messages, /api/brands JSON and XML, DELETE /api/brands, picture route, WebForms list/paging/CRUD including its legacy validation quirks.
  • Container images (aspnet:8.0) start healthy in mock and SQL profiles and replay with 0 failing flows.
  • .NET 8 test suites green (unit and integration, incl. SQL-backed unit tests against SQL Server 2022).

Known limitations / pre-existing legacy defects (reproduced deliberately)

  • D-01..D-04: host 404 error-page bodies differ (Mono/xsp4 vs ASP.NET Core); status codes equal.
  • Legacy defects Q1-Q18 preserved on purpose (see Q-PRE, L-01, L-02), e.g. unknown WebForms ids and pageSize=0 return 500, WebForms validators not enforced in mock mode.
  • K-01: legacy measured on Mono/xsp4, not IIS. K-02: container SQL data state compared via pages.
  • No recorded manual UI walkthrough (testing agent) in this automated run; UI evidence = Playwright screenshots in section 9 and the replayed transcripts.
  • CI parity gate: repo variable ESHOPNET8_PARITY_GATE is still unset (needs a maintainer).
